summary: The legal array contains at most ten promise-producing functions, while correctness depends on lazy invocation, one independent post-settlement timer per call, preserved array order, and symmetric fulfillment and rejection handling rather than scalable wall-clock growth.

workload_bound.source_constraint: functions.length is between one and ten and ms is between 10 and 500 milliseconds

replacement_checks.evidence: Array mapping performs one constant-work wrapper construction for each of n source functions; each wrapper invocation installs one two-branch promise continuation and at most one pending timer.

A deterministic fake scheduler verifies no eager calls, source invocation at wrapper call time, exactly one timer after either settlement path, the exact ms delay, independent repeated calls, and maximum-array behavior.
Authored cases cover fulfillment, rejection, mixed outcomes, simultaneous settlements, reverse completion order, structured values, minimum delay, maximum delay, and ten functions.
The exact native source is remotely Accepted under the provider timeout, and every wrapper creates its timer immediately after its finite source promise settles.
